* JSON path keys on Postgres are rendered inline (`data->>'key'`, `'{"a","b"}'::text[]`) instead of as bound parameters, so `GROUP BY` and `ORDER BY` on a JSON lookup work under psycopg3, which binds each as a distinct parameter.

* `exists()` wraps the query in `EXISTS(...)` rather than replacing its columns, fixing queries that order by or filter on a selected alias, and queries on MySQL that select two columns w/the same name.

Couple little things for `EnumField`. * `EnumField` and `IntEnumField` validate member value types (`str` and `int` respectively) at field construction. * `EnumField` and `IntEnumField` default `choices` to `(value, name)` pairs derived from the enum. * Fix #3075, migration generation for `EnumField`. Generated migrations will emit the storage field type (e.g. `IntegerField`) rather than `EnumField()`. [View commits](https://github.com/coleifer/peewee/compare/4.5.0...4.5.1)

* MySQL and MariaDB connections no longer set `sql_mode`. Peewee had been setting `PIPES_AS_CONCAT`, but the param replaced the server's mode rather than adding to it, which silently disabled `STRICT_TRANS_TABLES` (etc). Going forward Peewee will not modify `sql_mode` by default and use `CONCAT()` rather than `||` for MySQL/MariaDB.
* SQLite `BEGIN`, `COMMIT` and `ROLLBACK` are issued directly on a cursor rather than through `execute_sql()`, so they are no longer debug-logged, do not fire query hooks and ar

* Add `playhouse.migrations` for running migration scripts. Migrations are python files defining `up(migrator, db)` and optionally `down(...)`. Migrations are applied in numeric order a-la Django, and stored by name in a history table. CLI via `pwmigrate` accepting `status`, `up`, `down`, `initial`, `create`, `generate`, `fake` and `diff`. To run from python, `migrations.run(db)`.

Bug fixes for v3.1.0 (#127):

- `Nullable(String)` no longer panics on a nil `*string` or `*[]byte` in `AppendAny`; it appends null.
- An empty map is now checked by its key and value types, so a Variant sends it to the matching member (for example `[]map[string]string{}` to `Array(Map(String, String))`, not `Array(Map(String, Int64))`).
- Map and Array columns keep the right offsets when you append or delete after a read.
- `MapBase.ValidateInsert` now checks that offsets match the key and value rows, as A

Smaller builds: the column conversion methods (`Array`, `Nullable`, `LC`, `LowCardinality`, ...) are now Go 1.27 generic methods, so they no longer pull whole generic method sets into every importing package. Call sites stay the same. On a large codebase the test build cache dropped by more than half.

First public release. Hivemill is a self-hosted factory of Claude Code agents: you talk to one boss agent, and a team of coders, QA, reviewers and a judge ships your work as reviewed pull requests. See the README for the quickstart and the 76-second demo.

pg_lion is an inverted index for PostgreSQL built on compressed, roaring-style bitmaps. It answers counts, filters and `GROUP BY` from the index, usually without visiting the table, and also covers arrays, `jsonb` and full-text search. This is the first tagged release.
